messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT — high error rate & token surge on /v1/chat (fn-call, structured outputs). Severity: P2. Trigger: fn_call failures skyrocketing + sustained 2.5x token/sec.
alex: oncall here, ack. seeing large spike on us-east and eu-west. logs show lots of repeated tool-invoke retries and huge JSON blobs being generated. starting mitigation.
alex: quick heads-up: plan is to soft-gate function calls first, then restrict structured-output routes. want minimal customer impact -> prefer rate-limit over hard disable unless it gets worse.
alex: @tess can you join? need config push and to coordinate with customer-success for high-usage tenants.
tess: joining. bringing up dashboard now. can we get the list of tenants with >1000 fn_calls/min in the last 10m? mike can you dump from telemetry?
mike: pulling now. quick list: tenant-acme, tenant-zenith, tenant-scribe, a handful of SaaS test orgs. sending blob to #tmp in a sec. 
mike: dump: tenant-acme 2.4k/min fn_calls, tenant-zenith 1.1k/min, tenant-scribe 1.0k/min. top models: gpt-open-32k-qa (fn_call enabled) and redwood-llama-alpha (structured-json).
jenny: customer-impact heads-up: acme and scribe have active support chats. I'll loop them after we pick mitigation. priority: keep web app availability, degrade tool calling first.
alex: executing soft-gate step 1: reduce per-tenant fn_call QPS by 70% for non-enterprise tiers, keep enterprise grace. applying via internal admin API. command:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/quotas/adjust \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"tenant:nonenterprise","limit_adjust":{"fn_call_qps_multiplier":0.3}}'
```
alex: applied. monitoring.
alex: attaching quick watch query: http://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/fncall-errors?from=now-30m&to=now
alex: error rate dipped ~40% within 60s but token throughput still high. looks like structured outputs are the bigger cost.
tess: okay prepare step 2: selectively disable structured output (response_format=json) on the public streaming endpoint for non-enterprise tenants. I'll push a routing rule to rewrite incoming requests: if header X-Structured-Output:true and tenant != enterprise -> return 429 with guidance.
tess: patch command (dry-run first):
```
rwctl config set routing/structured_output_gate '{"mode":"soft","nonenterprise_action":"rate_limit_429","enterprise":"allow"}' --env prod
```
mike: lgtm. I'll apply in 30s and watch infra. deploying now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: routing/structured_output_gate -> prod (canary 5%)
alex: noticing a cluster of retries in logs from a subset of SDK versions that aggressively retry on 5xx. we should also add a temporary client-side guidance header to reduce retries.
jenny: messaging to customers: doing initial notify to acme + scribe that we may throttle some structured outputs to preserve latency. sending now.
jenny: message sent to acme + scribe support contacts. copy of message: "We are applying temporary limits to structured output and function calls to reduce latency spikes. Your app may receive 429s for structured responses; we recommend enabling exponential backoff for retries. We'll update in 30m."
alex: can we also blacklist inbound tool payloads that exceed 64KB? lots of malformed tool args causing runaway models.
tess: yes adding size gate: inbound_tool_payload_max_bytes=65536 via policy engine.
tess: policy applied. watch for 4xx from SDKs.
mike: immediate improvement: token/sec down ~55% and CPU on p3 nodes trending down. fn_call error rate now low but retry storms persist from older SDKs.
alex: okay hold on re-enabling any structured outputs until we confirm token economics. for now document mitigations so next oncall can keep them.
alex: mitigation summary (for handoff):
- reduced fn_call qps for non-enterprise to 30% of baseline
- soft-rate-limit structured outputs for non-enterprise -> return 429
- enforce inbound tool payload max 64KB
- notified affected customers (acme, scribe)
- monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds adjusted

alex: paging note: I'll hand off to @tess in 10m. please keep an eye on tenant-acme, they had the highest sustained use.

--- 10 minutes later ---

alex: handing over to tess. details above. slack thread pinned. leaving oncall.
tess: taking over. I'll keep the soft-gates for now, increase canary to 50% to ensure no regressions when we eventually relax. next steps: validate SDK behavior across versions, reach out to devex to draft retry guidance.
tess: I'm also opening a follow-up incident ticket to track root cause and long-term fixes: INC-2026-4539.

mike: note for postmortem: telemetry shows a correlation between a bot that started passing huge arrays in tool args (likely a customer-side misclient) and the spike. add rate-limits on array length.
jenny: support will follow up with affected customers and coordinate compensation if needed. sending an empathy + status update now.

alex: final status update: mitigations holding, token/sec back to ~baseline, will leave soft-gates for at least 2 hours and then evaluate. if anything changes I'll reopen page.
tess: thanks all. I'll own postmortem and rollback plan. closing thread for now. :thumbsup:
